subject: known incompatibility 10/11: heap-table row order
decision: HIT by construction (every table is a heap; no ORGANIZATION INDEX in 01_tables.sql / 02_horror.sql) and DISPOSITIONED: every embed element key in the patcher output sorts deterministically and is unique within its parent — invoices.lines key LINE_NO -> lineNo (UNIQUE uq_invoice_lines (invoice_id, line_no) 01_tables.sql:131; reader ORDER BY line_no 04_pkg_invoicing.sql:109, ap-620d0a2057); invoices.dunningAttempts key ID -> id (PK VARCHAR2(36); readers ORDER BY scheduled_for DESC, id DESC facade.py:346, ap-0a1051eac3); tenants.creditNotes key ID -> id (PK; reader ORDER BY issued_on, id 04_pkg_invoicing.sql:184, ap-b259650bfe); customerMaster.attributes key [ATTR_NAME, EAV_ID] -> [k, eavId] (EAV_ID is the PK; reader ORDER BY eav_id facade.py:296, ap-6c1786cb2d). Decision: the loader writes each embedded array sorted ascending by the element key, so a reload of the same source rows is byte-identical (idempotent) and never depends on Oracle heap scan order; the recon harness grades embed elements by element key, not position (tiers.py _grade_embeds). Root reads that relied on heap order without ORDER BY (05_pkg_dunning.sql:43-44, ap-37287a11b5; 04_pkg_invoicing.sql:59-60, ap-41de3e5203) are single-row aggregates and have no order dependency.

evidence.note: [d-known-incompat-heap-order] mapping_spec.json collections[*].embeds[*].key: 4 embeds (lines, dunningAttempts, creditNotes, attributes), 4 deterministic unique element keys

subject: known incompatibility 11/11: numbers rendered as text
decision: HIT in the read facades: reports.py:45,64-65,85-86 TO_CHAR(SUM(...),'FM999999999999990.00') and NVL(st.code_desc,'UNKNOWN('||TO_CHAR(h.status_cd)||')') (ap-6167f9171f, ap-89c88ad4c6, ap-c9b3d38c2c), reports.py:250 f"{total_amount:.2f}", backends/oracle.py:19-20 str(Decimal) with oracledb fetch_decimals=True (oracle_conn.py:5); in packages TO_CHAR(NVL(p_val,-1)) 01_pkg_util.sql:45 and TO_CHAR of line/attempt counters feeding f_md5_uuid (04_pkg_invoicing.sql:160, 05_pkg_dunning.sql:56). Decision: amounts load as Decimal128 at the declared scale (canonicalization decimal_round, numeric_abs_tol 0 in recon_tolerances.json) and counts/codes as int — never as strings or doubles; text rendering stays an application-tier concern at port time (format from the Decimal, FM...0.00 == two fixed decimals, integral NUMBER as str(int)). Recon compares numbers numerically on both sides, so no text-vs-number mismatch can be graded as parity.
